description: Public task corpus for the jcodemunch-mcp token-efficiency benchmark. Tasks are tool-agnostic: any code retrieval tool can be evaluated against the same queries and repos.

pinning.policy: Every repo carries the upstream commit SHA it was measured at. A run whose index reports a different git_head is measuring a different corpus and must not be compared to a published number. See benchmarks/REPRODUCING.md.
pinning.file_counts: Descriptions state no file count. The number of files a repo contributes depends on the indexing installation (grammar pack, size limits, skip patterns), not on the repo alone — the measured count lives in jcm_reference.json beside the SHA that produced it.

tasks.description: Find the core function or method responsible for registering and dispatching route handlers.
tasks.rationale: The most common agent entry point when exploring a web framework codebase.

tasks.description: Find middleware registration, chaining, or execution logic.
tasks.rationale: Middleware is a cross-cutting concern that spans multiple files in every web framework.

tasks.description: Find error handling, exception types, or error propagation logic.
tasks.rationale: Error handling is typically spread across several layers; tests retrieval across abstraction levels.

tasks.description: Find the request/response object definitions or wrappers.
tasks.rationale: Core types referenced throughout the codebase; high symbol density.

tasks.description: Find request parameter binding: the code that reads route, query or body parameters into the handler's arguments.
tasks.rationale: Tests retrieval of framework-specific patterns that differ significantly across languages.

methodology.baseline: Baseline A (read-all): concatenate all indexed source files and count tokens. This is a CEILING NOBODY PAYS - it assumes an agent opens every file in the repository before acting. Retained for continuity with published figures; it is not the number to quote.
methodology.jmunch_workflow: call search_symbols (max_results=5), then get_symbol for the top 3 hits. Total = search response tokens + 3 × symbol source tokens.
methodology.reduction_formula: (1 - jmunch_tokens / baseline_tokens) * 100, computed against each baseline separately and labelled. Quote the Baseline B figure.
methodology.note: Measured 2026-08-03 on the pinned corpus: Baseline B is 11.8% of Baseline A, so measuring against read-all overstates the advantage by roughly 8x. The aggregate ratio falls 237.3x -> 27.9x and the reduction 99.6% -> 96.4%. Per-query spread on B is 7.3x to 84.3x with a median of 25.5x; the read-all aggregate/median gap (237.3 vs 134.5) is far wider than B's (27.9 vs 25.5), so B is also much less distorted by the largest repo.
methodology.baseline_realistic: Baseline B (grep-top-3): what a competent agent WITHOUT the tool actually pays. `rg -l` the query's terms across the same indexed corpus (paths only), rank the matching files by match count, then open the top 3 in full. Total = file-list tokens + 3 whole files. Measured in the SAME run as the jCodeMunch side, never a stored constant.
methodology.baseline_choices: Every modelling choice in Baseline B is made in the BASELINE's favour, i.e. against jCodeMunch. (1) The grep cost is `rg -l`, paths only - the leanest real output. `rg` with matched lines is also measured (match_lines_tokens) and is strictly larger; using it would roughly double the baseline. (2) Files are ranked by match count, where real grep output has no ranking and the agent guesses. (3) Matching is case-insensitive substring on ANY term, the most permissive reading. Both baselines read through one shared reader, so the ratio between them describes two workflows and not two corpora.
methodology.disclosed_limit: Baseline B reads files WHOLE, because that is what agents do - this project's own PreToolUse hook exists to intercept whole-file Read calls. An agent that reads a line range pays less, and NO ESTIMATOR for that is offered: the removed size-proportional estimator in the comparison harnesses is why this project does not estimate an unmeasured side.
